subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) — Hosted vs Current Provider — Follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>, Samantha Ruiz <samantha@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) — Hosted vs Current Provider — Follow-up

Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment heading into a short PoC:  

Recap from call:
- Primary goals: reduce end-to-end latency for interactive chat features and support streaming outputs for long-form generation.
- Current constraints you called out: 4,000 concurrent chat sessions during peak, average request size ~600 tokens, and some long tail spikes during batch imports.
- Key SLOs you want to validate: p95 and p99 end-to-end latency (client -> host -> response), and consistent streaming chunk latency for streaming endpoints.

What we heard you need for qualification:
1) p95 (end-to-end) target: <= 350ms for the majority of interactive prompts.
2) p99 (end-to-end) target: <= 800ms for bursty traffic (ideally <= 500ms if possible).
3) Sustained throughput target: handle 4k concurrent sessions with median throughput of ~2 tokens/sec/session and occasional spikes up to 6 tokens/sec/session.
4) Streaming: per-chunk latency <= 100ms from first token to client while maintaining p95/p99 above.

Here’s how Redwood's hosted offering differs from your current provider (based on your notes + our follow-up):
- Current provider (Finlytics notes): p95 ~300–450ms typical, p99 ~1.0–1.4s during peaks; streaming lag often increases p99 by ~400–600ms.
- Redwood hosted (what we can target in a short PoC): p95 ~120–250ms, p99 ~300–600ms depending on prompt length and concurrency; streaming chunk latency typically <= 80–120ms.

We’ll validate using a small PoC with synthetic traffic derived from your anonymized traces (thanks for sending the trace files). Proposed scope for the PoC (2 weeks):
- Week 1: baseline benchmark on hosted API using configuration A (default batching), measure p95/p99 across a sample of ~10k requests and a concurrency sweep to 4k sessions.
- Week 2: tuning (batching, prefix caching, lightweight quantization) and run streaming tests to measure per-chunk latency and p99 tail.

Next steps / asks from your side:
- Confirm the targets above (p95/p99 and streaming per-chunk latency) — if different, reply with numbers; we’ll tune accordingly.
- Provide a short sample of anonymized production traces or attach the export to HubSpot (we received the ZIP but want a sample labeled traffic.json if possible).
- Confirm the contact for procurement/POC approvals (who should we loop in on the trial contract).

I attached a short benchmark summary that shows typical host vs provider comparisons for workloads similar to yours — we’ll run the PoC against your traces and share a full report.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning on targets and kicking off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) — Hosted vs Current Provider — Follow-up

Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed recap. That matches our internal notes. A couple clarifications so we can lock targets for the POA:  

1) The p95 target of <=350ms is what we’ve told engineering as a stretch; the business would be happy with p95 <=250ms if attainable without large cost increases.
2) For p99, our current internal SLA asks for <=800ms; we’d be happy to see Redwood hit <=500ms in a PoC to consider upsell.
3) On streaming, the critical metric is time-to-first-token (startup latency) — we need first-token <=120ms 95% of the time and chunk latency <=150ms for subsequent chunks.
4) Concurrency: 4k concurrent sessions is realistic for peak; we can provide a 24-hour sample where typical concurrency is ~1.2k and spikes to 4k for 15–30 minutes.

I uploaded a sanitized trace bundle to the HubSpot record and attached a smaller sample to this thread (finlytics-call-traces-20270214.zip). If you need specific endpoints or prompt mixes let us know and we’ll label them.

Procurement: loop in our procurement lead, Samantha (cc’d), for trial terms. For PoC approvals, we can sign a short trial order covering dedicated test windows.

Appreciate it — if Redwood can demonstrate p95 <=250ms and p99 <=500ms for our typical load with streaming first-token <=120ms, we’ll be in a strong position to proceed.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product — Finlytics
alex@finlytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finlytics.com>
Cc: Samantha Ruiz <samantha@finlytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) — Hosted vs Current Provider — Follow-up

Alex / Sam —

Perfect — that gives us clear targets to validate. Quick notes on how we’ll approach the PoC to reach those numbers:  

- Baseline config: Redwood hosted API w/ dynamic batching + prefix KV caching enabled. For your average prompt (600 tokens) we expect p95 in the 140–220ms range at moderate concurrency and p99 under 500ms after tuning.
- Streaming: our runtime prioritizes first-token delivery via low-latency kernels and micro-batching; most customers see first-token <=80–110ms on hosted, with subsequent chunk latencies ~40–100ms.
- Concurrency tuning: we’ll run a concurrency sweep (1k -> 4k) and adjust batching window to keep per-request latency within SLOs while sustaining throughput.

I’ve attached the short benchmark summary we touched on in the call. For the PoC we propose:
1) Redwood runs initial baseline using your uploaded sample traces (we’ll start with the 24-hour typical window, then reproduce spike windows).
2) We’ll share a P95/P99 report within 4 business days of starting the baseline.
3) After tuning we’ll run the final tests and deliver a full report and recommended config for production (routing policies, cache policies, and batching parameters).

Can we lock start of PoC next Monday (Feb 22)? Also, we’ll need a short signed trial order (SLA-free, limited test credits). Samantha — could you confirm procurement cadence and any legal redlines we should expect?

If that works I’ll get the kick-off plan in a calendar invite and request the sample trace file labeled traffic.json from the ZIP.

Thanks —
Marissa
